proposed_method: Fuel Cs-137 (Bq/kg dry) = deposition density (Task 1.7 baselines: weapons fallout and Chernobyl, kBq/m2 by country) x aggregated transfer factor Tag(t) (m2/kg), with Tag(t) rising to a peak 10-16 y after deposition and then falling (S0544, S0543). Tag bounds 1e-4 to 5.5e-3 m2/kg (S0548 low end, Fukushima; S0543 high end, Polissya). Cross-check against measured regional ranges: Sweden 1997 wood 3-300 (S0515, S0536); Ukraine firewood <2-690 (S0539); Austria 2020-22 mean 2.1 (S0530); Lithuania imports <=156 (S0514); Poland 0.15-3.7 (S0535).
notes: Zero by physics (inference); marked no_data for consistency with the Task 1.6 file. No Cs-137 in fuel before the first fallout. 1950s-1980s: no wood measurement found; only the US ash survey (S0520, ash 2.9-780 Bq/kg, weapons fallout, sampled 1990-92) and the Fukushima-era Tag as proxies. Chernobyl-era wood (1986-89): only Swedish pine shoots 1986-91 (S0536). Trade breaks the link between country of use and country of origin (S0534, S0514).

proposed_method: Ash Cs-137 = fuel Cs-137 x ash concentration factor (ACF, dry fuel to ash). ACF = 1 / ash yield x retention. Household wood ash yield about 1% (S0515, S0520, S0536); bark 3-5%, stemwood about 0.5% (S0536); charcoal 3% (S0564). Observed ACF: 77-209 fireplaces, 107-118 stoves, 85 pellet stove (K-40 based, S0531); Austria 58 chips, 181 pellets, 144 briquettes, 348 single log (S0530); Sweden houses about 91 (S0515); Lithuania 95-370 (S0514); Zhytomyr 50-100 (S0516); Netherlands/Belgium 70 to over 200 (S0538). Use 50-370 with central about 100 (modelled central pending calibration).
notes: Measured ash: Sweden houses 1997 2-21 kBq/kg, soot 2-23 kBq/kg (S0515); Zhytomyr 2017 170-32,900 Bq/kg (S0516); Austria 2020-22 11.8-867 (S0530); Greece 2013 25-499 (S0531); US 1990-92 2.9-780 (S0520). Before 1990 no household ash measurement found.

proposed_method: Charcoal concentration C_char = C_wood x r_c / y_c, where y_c is the carbonisation mass yield (S0563, not yet read) and r_c the fraction of wood Cs-137 kept in char (about 0.98 at 300 C, 0.75-0.85 at 350-450 C, 0.65-0.70 above 500 C, from the S0551 lab test on cedar bark; kiln value unmeasured). Natural nuclides: concentrated by 1 / y_c, assuming no loss for K-40, Ra and Th (inference; Pb-210 and Po-210 volatile, treat as for combustion). Japanese indicator 280 Bq/kg (S0560) is a limit, not a measurement.
notes: No measured radionuclide concentration in charcoal from any country found; none for Africa or Asia. Rows are no_data for every decade; proposed method applies from the 1960s for Cs-137 and from pre1950 for natural nuclides.
